name: ping
title: Ping (user)
description: Returns 'pong'. Smoke test that the user MCP endpoint is reachable.

name: bulk_apply
title: Bulk Apply
description: Apply multiple record changes atomically via POST /api/operations (JSON:API Atomic Operations). All operations succeed together or none do. Use this for multi-record changes that must roll back as a unit (e.g. moving line items between orders, rewiring relationships).

operations.description: Ordered list of operations. Applied as a single transaction — all succeed or all roll back.

items.description: One operation. {"op":"add"|"update"|"remove", "type":"<collection>", "id":"<id>" (required for update/remove; a "lid" from an earlier add works too), "lid":"<local-id>" (optional on add — lets later operations reference the new record), "attributes":{...} (for add/update), "relationships":{...} (optional for add/update)}

name: create_record
title: Create Record
description: Create a single record in a collection. Wraps POST /api/{collection} in JSON:API format. Returns the created record on success (HTTP 201).

attributes.description: Field values for the new record, keyed by field name. Reference get_collection_schema to know what fields exist.

relationships.description: Optional JSON:API relationships object. Each entry maps a relationship name to {"data": {"type": "...", "id": "..."}} or an array thereof for to-many.

name: delete_record
title: Delete Record
description: Delete a single record. Wraps DELETE /api/{collection}/{id}. Returns 204 No Content on success. Idempotent — deleting a non-existent record returns 404.

name: describe_api
title: Describe API
description: Return the auto-generated OpenAPI 3.0 spec for the current tenant: JSON:API CRUD paths and schemas for every collection, including system collections. Specialized controllers (flows, approvals, bulk) are NOT in this spec; use the dedicated tools for those. For one collection's field list, types, enums and validation rules, use get_collection_schema instead of parsing this spec. Example: call with no arguments, then look up the "/accounts" path in the returned "paths" object for its exact request/response shape.

name: execute_flow
title: Execute Flow
description: Trigger a flow execution. Returns the execution id; use get_flow_run to poll status. Inputs must be double-wrapped: execute_flow(flowId, input={"input": {"slug": "x"}}) so the flow can read $.input.slug. See integrations.md "Flows" for the state envelope.

flowId.description: Flow id (UUID) or name. Wraps POST /api/flows/{flowId}/execute.

input.description: Optional HTTP request body. Must double-wrap the flow's input under an "input" key: pass {"input": {"slug": "x"}} so the engine's state envelope sets $.input = {"slug": "x"} and the flow can read $.input.slug. Single-wrapping (e.g. {"slug": "x"}) leaves $.input empty and downstream tasks fail with confusing errors.

name: get_collection_schema
title: Get Collection Schema
description: Return the full schema for a collection: metadata + all field definitions (type, required, enum values, references, systemMaintained) plus its validation rules by default. PICKLIST and MULTI_PICKLIST fields carry picklistValues — the active values, each {value, label, isDefault, sortOrder}, in sortOrder — so write one of those values instead of guessing. Wraps GET /api/collections/{name}/schema, and — when includeRules is true — GET /api/validation-rules for that collection. Use this before constructing a query or create_record call to know what attributes are available; a systemMaintained field is set by flows only, and a create or update that sets or changes it returns 400. Example: {"collection": "accounts"} returns accounts' fields with types/enums and its active validation rules.

collection.description: Collection name or ID (e.g. "accounts" or a UUID). Looked up via /api/collections.

includeRules.description: Also fetch and embed the collection's validation rules (default true).

name: get_flow_run
title: Get Flow Run
description: Fetch the status of a flow execution. Wraps GET /api/flows/executions/{executionId}, with optional step-by-step logs from /steps merged in. Use to poll a long-running flow.

executionId.description: Flow execution id returned by execute_flow.

includeSteps.description: If true, also fetch step-level execution logs and merge them into the response.

name: get_record
title: Get Record
description: Fetch a single record by id from a collection. Returns the JSON:API single-resource response.

id.description: Record id (UUID), or display field value if the collection has one (e.g. email for users).

include.description: Comma-separated relationship names to include in the response.

name: list_approvals
title: List Approvals
description: List approval instances, optionally filtered by status. Wraps the approvalInstances system collection. Useful to find what's waiting on you.

name: list_collections
title: List Collections
description: List all collections available in the current tenant. Returns JSON:API formatted list with collection metadata. Use this to discover what data is available before querying.

includeSystem.description: Include system collections (users, fields, layouts, etc.). Default true.

name: list_notifications
title: List Notifications
description: List your own in-app notifications, newest first. Wraps GET /api/me/notifications; meta.unreadCount carries your unread total. Use mark_notification_read to mark one read.

name: mark_notification_read
title: Mark Notification Read
description: Mark one of your in-app notifications read. Wraps POST /api/me/notifications/{id}/read; returns the notification and meta.unreadCount. Repeating the call keeps the first read time.

id.description: Id of one of your notifications (from list_notifications).

name: query_collection
title: Query Collection

filter.description:
{ field: { OP: value } }. Ops on one field AND together (ranges); fields AND across; NO OR.
Supported: EQ NEQ GT GTE LT LTE CONTAINS STARTS ENDS ICONTAINS ISTARTS IENDS IEQ ISNULL IN.
IN value is a CSV string or array, e.g. "a,b" or ["a","b"].
Workarounds: BETWEEN→GTE+LTE; STARTSWITH/ENDSWITH→STARTS/ENDS; IS_NULL→ISNULL; OR→multiple queries.
Ex: { "status": { "EQ": "ACTIVE" }, "createdAt": { "GTE": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" } }

sort.description: CSV sort keys; '-' prefix = desc. Ex: "-createdAt,lastName".

pageSize.description: Records per page (default 20, max 200). Use 1 to fetch only meta.totalCount.

fields.description: Sparse fieldset — CSV attribute names. Default: all. Ex: "firstName,lastName,email".

include.description: CSV relationship names to eager-load (returned in top-level included[]). Ex: "account,owner".

name: search
title: Search
description: Cross-collection full-text search. Returns hits with collection name, record id, and matched snippet. Useful when you don't know which collection holds the answer.

query.description: Free-text query (matches against searchable fields across all collections).

name: semantic_search
title: Semantic Search
description: Vector similarity search over a collection's VECTOR field. Wraps POST /api/{collection}/semantic-search; returns the nearest records by cosine distance, with per-record distances under meta. Prefer this over `search` when ranking by meaning rather than keyword match.

collection.description: Collection name to search; it must define a VECTOR field.

query.description: Natural-language text; records are ranked by semantic similarity to it.

name: submit_for_approval
title: Submit for Approval
description: Submit a record for approval. Wraps POST /api/approvals/submit. Returns the new approval instance id; use list_approvals to track its status.

collectionId.description: Collection id (UUID) of the record being submitted. Use get_collection_schema to look up by name.

recordId.description: Record id to submit for approval.

processId.description: Optional approval process id. If omitted, the platform auto-selects a matching process.

name: update_record
title: Update Record
description: Update fields on a single record. Wraps PATCH /api/{collection}/{id}. Only the attributes you supply are modified — omitted fields keep their current values.

id.description: Record id (UUID or display field value).

attributes.description: Field values to update. Only the keys you include are modified — other fields are untouched (PATCH semantics).

relationships.description: Optional JSON:API relationships object to replace; each entry maps a relationship name to a JSON:API resource identifier.
